chamber.rule: 51 of 100 seats, or 50 with the Vice President's vote; seats not up and independents counted by caucus

vice_president.note: the Vice President is elected the same day; until D1's published presidential win probability is in, 0.5, assumed independent of the Senate swing

chamber.not_up_source: the winner of each seat's latest election before 2008: Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder from 2006, MEDSL's U.S. Senate 1976-2024 before

notes: 1. Vacancy in Minnesota's Class 2 seat owing to contested election. Both Independent senators caucused with the Democrats.
2. Arlen Specter of Pennsylvania changed his party affiliation from Republican to Democratic.
3. Al Franken (D) of Minnesota was seated after resolution of contested election, filling the Class 2 vacancy.
4. Scott Brown (R) of Massachusetts, elected January 19, 2010, was seated, replacing appointed Senator Paul Kirk (D).
5. Mark Kirk (R) of Illinois, elected November 2, 2010, was seated, replacing appointed Senator Roland Burris (D).
